problems.title: The fractional-trust threshold lies in the wrong interval
problems.source_location: Lemma A.1(3), PDF pp.20–21; Section 2, PDF p.5
claim: Lemma A.1(3) places the zero-growth forecast error \(\epsilon^*(\lambda)\) in \((0,1/2)\) for its stated fractional-trust range.
analysis: At \(\lambda=1/2\), correct and incorrect predictions give wealth factors \(13/8\) and \(7/8\). Chance-level expected log growth is \(\tfrac12\log(91/64)>0\). Since growth decreases linearly in the prediction-error probability, the root is \(\log(13/8)/[\log(13/8)-\log(7/8)]\approx0.78429\), above \(1/2\). More generally the interior range \(1/3<\lambda<1\) has its root in \((1/2,1)\).
result: The below-chance fragility interpretation of this lemma is incorrect. The RAM guarantee is a separate statement.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Use the actual logarithmic root and distinguish the endpoints \(\lambda=1/3\) and \(\lambda=1\). Fractional trust can retain positive growth at chance-level forecasts in this two-asset example.
problems.impact_rationale: This is an ancillary motivating lemma, not a counterexample to the principal online protection result.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Ranking groups do not match the row order
problems.source_location: Section 3, PDF pp.9–10, Table 4; official notebook cells 34–35
claim: The official notebook’s `prepare_long` and `build_lgb_dataset`, cell 34, are intended to form one cross-sectional ranking query per date.
analysis: The melt operation yields asset-major rows, but the supplied group sizes assume contiguous same-date rows. In a complete panel of three assets and four dates, the first size-three query contains the first asset on dates one through three rather than three assets on one date. Labels, features and weights therefore enter the wrong query grouping.
result: The notebook’s ranking interface is inconsistent. The published wealth values are not recalculated or directly contradicted.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Sort the entire feature/label/weight table by date before splitting arrays and constructing consecutive query groups. This repairs membership without claiming recovered investment performance.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a released data-grouping error with unquantified central experimental impact.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: The geometric-mean floor does not imply BCRP universality
problems.source_location: Theorem 2.1, PDF p.6; introduction/discussion protection interpretation
analysis: With constant two-asset returns \((2,1/2)\) and consistently wrong ranks, the stated RAM behavior cycles to wealth \(1\) at even horizons, whereas the best constant rebalanced portfolio attains \(2^n\). This separates the geometric-mean comparator from a sublinear log-regret guarantee against BCRP.
result: Theorem 2.1 remains valid in this example. It should be interpreted with its proved comparator.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
problems.impact_rationale: This is comparator clarification, not a supported error in the formal guarantee.
problems.existing_correction_status: Scope clarification only; no author-paper repair or adoption is asserted.
